### BoK Gate check (v3 — MCORCH Master Execution Protocol)

For each BoK suite in `docs/bok/<slug>/`, verify completeness:
```bash
for slug in $(ls docs/bok/ 2>/dev/null); do
  if [ "$slug" = "security" ]; then
    required_sec=(00-deepsearch-blueprint 01-brd-security 02-srs-secure-spec 03-sdd-hardening-architecture 04-fmea-security)
    missing=()
    for doc in "${required_sec[@]}"; do
      [ -f "docs/bok/security/$doc.md" ] || missing+=("$doc")
    done
    [ ${#missing[@]} -eq 0 ] && echo "✅ security — BoK complete (ciso-4-artifact)" || echo "⚠️ security — missing: ${missing[*]}"
    continue
  fi
  required=(00-index 01-mrd 02-brd 03-prd 04-frd 05-sdd 06-data-model 07-process-flow 08-quality-metrics)
  missing=()
  for doc in "${required[@]}"; do
    [ -f "docs/bok/$slug/$doc.md" ] || missing+=("$doc")
  done
  [ ${#missing[@]} -eq 0 ] && echo "✅ $slug — BoK complete" || echo "⚠️ $slug — missing: ${missing[*]}"
done
```

If the user mentions working on a **new module / complex feature / integration / architectural change**:
- Check whether `docs/bok/<expected-slug>/` exists with all 9 docs.
- If missing: surface in the **ALERTAS** section as a critical block per CLAUDE.md MCORCH Master Execution Protocol.
- Recommend `/bok-scribe <idea summary>` before any code is written.

## Rules

- **TypeScript errors → report immediately.** If there are TS errors, list them under ALERTAS. Do not start implementing new features until errors are resolved (unless the user explicitly asks to proceed despite errors).
- **Unhealthy containers → report with triage.** Suggest the fix command if known (e.g., `docker compose restart mcorch-vector-engine` for chroma).
- **Uncommitted changes → describe, do not commit.** Only describe what exists in the working tree; committing is the user's call.
- **Keep the brief tight.** No padding. No repetition of CLAUDE.md architecture. The user already knows the architecture — they need the delta: what changed, what's broken, what's next.
- **Pending Actions priority order:** CRITICAL (before first client) > NON-CRITICAL > Phase Zeta > Core v3 > Epsilon v9.
- **Knowledge Mesh numbers:** use `GraphRAG State` section from HANDOFF.md as the source. Do not invent counts.

> ## Pipeline stages (per the n8n graph)
> 
> 1. **Scene script (Gemini 2.5 Flash)** → returns JSON array of 4 scenes; each: `{scene, narration (1-3 sentences),
>    image_prompt (cinematic 16:9), ambience (one of waves|wind|birds|city|forest|rain|keyboard|ambient),
>    hud (≤5-word on-screen caption)}`. Creative-director system prompt, faceless educational channel angle.
> 2. **Per-scene image (Pollinations)** → `image.pollinations.ai/prompt/<enc(image_prompt)>?width=1920&height=1080&nologo=true`.
> 3. **Per-scene narration (VoxCPM HF Space)** → `openbmb-voxcpm-demo.hf.space/gradio_api/call/generate`, SSE result
>    parsed for the audio URL; voice prompt = "Confident, warm male narrator… documentary tone". Download → `scene<N>.wav`.
> 4. **Probe audio duration** (`ffprobe` on the .wav) → drives each scene's frame count / clip length.
> 5. **Per-scene animation (LTX i2v)** → `node ltx.js <scene>` animates the still image → motion clip (image-to-video).
> 6. **Per-scene HUD overlay (Remotion)** → POST `remotion-render:8088/render` composition `SceneOverlay` codec=prores
>    (alpha .mov), props `{audioSrc, hudLabel, hudTitle, hudStat, captionText, accent:#F5C542}` — sci-fi FUI/HUD.
> 7. **Composite scene (FFmpeg)** → `composite.sh <scene> <ambience> <dur>` layers image/clip + audio + HUD + ambience → `scene<N>.mp4`.
> 8. **Concat (FFmpeg)** → `ls scene[0-9].mp4 | sort -V | … concat -c:v libx264 -crf 20 -preset medium -c:a aac -b:a 192k -movflags +faststart base.mp4`.
> 9. **Captions + HUD tracks** → JS builds **ASS karaoke** (`{\kNN}` per word, DejaVu Sans 54, gold #F5C542) from
>    narration + per-scene durations, and a **HUD .srt** from the `hud` fields.
> 10. **Polish (FFmpeg)** → `eq=contrast=1.08:saturation=1.12:brightness=0.012,vignette=PI/5` → `final.mp4`.
> 11. **QA vision gate (Gemini 2.5 Flash, multimodal)** → builds a **contact sheet** (`fps=12/D,scale=480,tile=3x4`),
>     sends it + script to a **senior motion-design award-critic** prompt (7 weighted dims: style_match, motion/easing,
>     typography, compositing/light-wrap, restraint, pacing/retention, brand) → verdict PASS|REVISE|REJECT + score/100
>     + ai-slop flags + ranked fixes + one trend-forward suggestion. (This is the same spirit as our Vision QA gate.)
> 12. **Deliver** → Telegram `sendVideo` with the QA caption. (Native: → social publish per objective.)
> 
> ## Native mapping (what to build under engine=faceless)

> | n8n leg | Native MCORCH |
> |---|---|
> | Gemini scenes / QA vision | per-user BYOK `google_api_key` (Vision MCP / our gemini path) — NOT a hardcoded key |

> | LTX i2v / Remotion HUD | our render-core (Playwright+FFmpeg) + HyperFrames compositions (the HUD = a HyperFrames layer) |
> | FFmpeg composite/concat/polish | render-core / a faceless worker (FFmpeg already on host) — the **long-form** capability |
> | ASS karaoke + HUD srt | deterministic caption builder (port the JS) |
> | Telegram deliver | `publish-meta` / `publish-social` per objective |

> Every produced asset (scene image, scene audio, scene clip, final mp4) → the **`creative_assets`** registry

# agent-browser

Fast browser automation CLI for AI agents. Chrome/Chromium via CDP with
accessibility-tree snapshots and compact `@eN` element refs.

Install: `npm i -g agent-browser && agent-browser install`

## Start here

This file is a discovery stub, not the usage guide. Before running any
`agent-browser` command, load the actual workflow content from the CLI:

```bash
agent-browser skills get core             # start here — workflows, common patterns, troubleshooting
agent-browser skills get core --full      # include full command reference and templates
```

The CLI serves skill content that always matches the installed version,
so instructions never go stale. The content in this stub cannot change
between releases, which is why it just points at `skills get core`.

## Specialized skills

Load a specialized skill when the task falls outside browser web pages:

```bash
agent-browser skills get electron          # Electron desktop apps (VS Code, Slack, Discord, Figma, ...)
agent-browser skills get slack             # Slack workspace automation
agent-browser skills get dogfood           # Exploratory testing / QA / bug hunts
agent-browser skills get vercel-sandbox    # agent-browser inside Vercel Sandbox microVMs
agent-browser skills get agentcore         # AWS Bedrock AgentCore cloud browsers
```

Run `agent-browser skills list` to see everything available on the
installed version.

## Why agent-browser

- Fast native Rust CLI, not a Node.js wrapper
- Works with any AI agent (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, Continue, Windsurf, etc.)
- Chrome/Chromium via CDP with no Playwright or Puppeteer dependency
- Accessibility-tree snapshots with element refs for reliable interaction
- Sessions, authentication vault, state persistence, video recording
- Specialized skills for Electron apps, Slack, exploratory testing, cloud providers

## Observability Dashboard

The dashboard runs independently of browser sessions on port 4848 and can also be opened through a proxied or forwarded URL such as `https://dashboard.agent-browser.localhost`. Agents should stay on the dashboard origin: session tabs, status, and stream traffic are proxied internally, so session ports do not need to be exposed.


ARGUMENTS: open YouTube embed player and capture screenshots at multiple seek positions

> ---
> name: core
> description: Core agent-browser usage guide. Read this before running any agent-browser commands. Covers the snapshot-and-ref workflow, navigating pages, interacting with elements (click, fill, type, select), extracting text and data, taking screenshots, managing tabs, handling forms and auth, waiting for content, running multiple browser sessions in parallel, and troubleshooting common failures. Use when the user asks to interact with a website, fill a form, click something, extract data, take a screenshot, log into a site, test a web app, or automate any browser task.
> allowed-tools: Bash(agent-browser:*), Bash(npx agent-browser:*)

> 
> # agent-browser core
> 
> Fast browser automation CLI for AI agents. Chrome/Chromium via CDP, no
> Playwright or Puppeteer dependency. Accessibility-tree snapshots with compact
> `@eN` refs let agents interact with pages in ~200-400 tokens instead of
> parsing raw HTML.
> 
> Most normal web tasks (navigate, read, click, fill, extract, screenshot) are
> covered here. Load a specialized skill when the task falls outside browser
> web pages — see [When to load another skill](#when-to-load-another-skill).
> 
> ## The core loop
> 
> ```bash
> agent-browser open <url>        # 1. Open a page
> agent-browser snapshot -i       # 2. See what's on it (interactive elements only)
> agent-browser click @e3         # 3. Act on refs from the snapshot
> agent-browser snapshot -i       # 4. Re-snapshot after any page change
> ```
> 
> Refs (`@e1`, `@e2`, ...) are assigned fresh on every snapshot. They become
> **stale the moment the page changes** — after clicks that navigate, form
> submits, dynamic re-renders, dialog opens. Always re-snapshot before your
> next ref interaction.
> 
> ## Quickstart
> 
> ```bash
> # Install once
> npm i -g agent-browser && agent-browser install
> 
> # Take a screenshot of a page
> agent-browser open https://example.com
> agent-browser screenshot home.png
> agent-browser close
> 
> # Search, click a result, and capture it
> agent-browser open https://duckduckgo.com
> agent-browser snapshot -i                      # find the search box ref
> agent-browser fill @e1 "agent-browser cli"
> agent-browser press Enter
> agent-browser wait --load networkidle
> agent-browser snapshot -i                      # refs now reflect results
> agent-browser click @e5                        # click a result
> agent-browser screenshot result.png
> ```
> 
> The browser stays running across commands so these feel like a single
> session. Use `agent-browser close` (or `close --all`) when you're done.
> 
> ## Reading a page
> 
> ```bash
> agent-browser snapshot                    # full tree (verbose)
> agent-browser snapshot -i                 # interactive elements only (preferred)
> agent-browser snapshot -i -u              # include href urls on links
> agent-browser snapshot -i -c              # compact (no empty structural nodes)
> agent-browser snapshot -i -d 3            # cap depth at 3 levels
> agent-browser snapshot -s "#main"         # scope to a CSS selector
> agent-browser snapshot -i --json          # machine-readable output
> ```
> 
> Snapshot output looks like:
> 
> ```
> Page: Example - Log in
> URL: https://example.com/login
> 
> @e1 [heading] "Log in"
> @e2 [form]
>   @e3 [input type="email"] placeholder="Email"
>   @e4 [input type="password"] placeholder="Password"
>   @e5 [button type="submit"] "Continue"
>   @e6 [link] "Forgot password?"
> ```

**Manter o Canvas Studio como corpo, renomeá-lo "Spaces", e portar para dentro dele a espinha de engenharia do módulo Spaces atual.** O achado mais importante da auditoria: isso **não contradiz** a BoK selada — é o **retorno ao contrato**. A `docs/bok/spaces-evolution/00-index.md` sempre disse que o Spaces deveria *"unificar os dois grafos já existentes (orchestrator/ e canvas/) sob um único Core"* e que *"Spaces o generaliza, não o substitui"*. Construir o `/dashboard/spaces` como módulo paralelo foi o descarrilamento que você percebeu.

## 📊 As provas materiais (workflow `wf_48351b58`, 6 agentes + crítico adversarial que verificou 4/4 claims no código e no DB vivo)

| Dimensão | Canvas Studio | Spaces |
|---|---|---|
| Uso real (DB vivo, count=exact) | **8 projetos reais** — "Gabriel AI" editado **hoje**, moodboards "5 mundos", campanha Samsung; 178 execuções | **3 rows, TODAS fixtures de E2E** ("E2E 2a/2c/2d"); 6 generations, todas de teste — **zero uso orgânico** |
| Código | ~8.000 LOC, **7 tipos de nó** (imagem, mood-board facial, compose 3-entradas, style transfer, vídeo, voz, avatar), previews na face do nó, reference threading (consistência visual), estilo por projeto, Realtime | ~2.250 LOC, cards de texto sem preview, 5 de 26 tipos executáveis |
| O que o Spaces tem de MELHOR | — | **Billing ledger-first** (débito+row numa transação, idempotência, refund automático anti-mint), **Estimar == cobrança real (gate G7)**, Spotlight com portas tipadas, histórico de geração por nó |

Consolidar não perde nada: os dois já compartilham o mesmo `canvas-execute`, webhook, bucket e spine `creative_assets`. Migrar dados = 3 rows de teste. **Bônus do crítico: achou um bug vivo de preço** — o nó sceneCompose mostra **18 mco** na face e no Run-All mas o servidor cobra **10** (`estimateNodeCost` lê custo stale do jsonb). É exatamente a classe de bug que o padrão G7 do Spaces elimina — mais um argumento para portar o ledger.

## 🎬 O que o vídeo do Magnific ensina (assistido frame a frame)

O YouTube bloqueou o IP do servidor em todas as camadas (yt-dlp, embed, playback), então extraí os **86 frames do storyboard** pelo seu Chrome conectado + enumerei a **playlist de 14 tutoriais** da Magnific Academy — que é o mapa de features completo do produto deles: nós+busca, conexões tipadas, **Assistant que monta o workflow por chat**, gerar/editar imagem, **Variations**, **Lists** (listas como nós = lote), imagem→vídeo, combinar/upscale vídeo, **extrair frames de vídeo**, áudio, referências→workflow, colaboração, **Designer Node** e **Flows** (seus workflows viram nós reutilizáveis).

O vídeo específico mostra o padrão-ouro: **Logo + Lista de produtos (moto, jet-ski, snowmobile) + Lista de textos → Designer Node (editor Figma-lite embutido) → N artes finais geradas automaticamente de UM template** ("FOR THE ROAD / FOR THE WATER / FOR THE SNOW"). Isso é **template × dados → lote de criativos** — nós já temos as peças (open-design, HyperFrames determinístico, reshaper data-driven, canvas-campaign-build.ts); o que falta é ligá-las como nós no canvas. Importante: a MRD selada **proíbe clonar a estética** da Magnific — mecânica sim, visual = MIV cyan.

## 🗺️ Plano Spaces v2 (fases, cada uma com gate)

1. **Fase 0 — Amendment 14 na BoK** (Closed-Loop Step 3.5) + **fix imediato do preço do sceneCompose** (1 linha, produção hoje).
2. **Fase 1 — Rename & takeover**: `/dashboard/canvas` → `/dashboard/spaces` (redirects), nav vira um "Spaces" único com sub-itens Studio/Design/Vídeo/Assets, aposentar as 2 páginas do Spaces atual (só 5 referências no src + 1 QA script).
3. **Fase 2 — Espinha de dinheiro**: portar ledger-first pro cliente Canvas (armadilhas mapeadas: FK composta das RPCs, mirror-parity test que parseia o source do edge fn, smokes pinados, estender o watchdog cron ao `generations`). `/security-review` obrigatório.
4. **Fase 3 — Polish Magnific-grade**: fundir Spotlight+portas tipadas no registry do Canvas, Estimar antes de rodar, cluster de histórico por nó, thumbnails reais nos cards da home (schema existe, falta o write-path), galeria de templates.
5. **Fase 4 — Lists + Designer Node**: o primitivo de lote + editor embutido data-driven — **essa é a alavanca de qualidade dos criativos** que você pediu.

## 📱 Perfis novos (curiosidades / filosofia milionária)

Não precisa esperar o Spaces v2: o **Viral Autopilot já roda sem produto** (fallback sem injeção de afiliado existe) e o motor HyperFrames tem os 2 templates (9:16 e 16:9). O caminho curto: criar a conta nova → OAuth em `social_credentials` → um `autopilot_plans` com persona/nicho próprio e **CTA de afiliado desligado até X seguidores** → cadência automática com Vision QA já ativo. Quando bater o limiar, liga o link-forge com `affiliate_tag` per-user. A qualidade visual dos criativos sobe de verdade na Fase 4 (template × lista, estilo consistente por perfil).

**Aguardando seu GO para a Fase 0** (amendment + fix do preço) — a partir daí executo fase a fase.
